title: Tracing and Filtering Unsupported Biomedical Extractions in a 55.5-Million-Relation Corpus
content: Background. Automated biomedical relations can reproduce source-selection and generation errors at scale. Methods. We audited 55,545,265 HCC v1.0 rows, standardized longitudinal labels by source, and extended an initial temporal diagnostic with 1,000 new sampled documents. Archived extractor inputs were recovered for 1,012 of 1,030 documents including discovery cases. We replayed a retained checkpoint on 70 new inputs and evaluated a fixed lexical rejection rule. Results. The unspecified-study share rose 22.13 percentage points in 2020, versus 1.92 with fixed source weights. Among 299 recovered pre-2019 holdout inputs, no tested COVID-family term occurred, yet the released outputs contained 380 explicit COVID-family rows. The gate rejected all 380. Replay generated 51 such rows from 30 held-out temporal inputs and matched all released tuples for 62 of 70 replayed documents overall. Generalstratum row retention ranged from 77.2% to 86.3%. One of 829 deliberately mismatched-input controls passed. In the post-2020 comparison, 56 of 529 COVID-labelled rows also lacked the tested term family in the archived input. Conclusions. Input-level replay localizes an unsupported-generation failure in inspected cases; a transparent lexical safeguard suppresses these outputs with measurable loss of coverage. Lexical retention is not semantic accuracy or clinical validation.
